page: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 64 virtual CPUs (32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled) running at 3.6 GHz, backed by 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz. This configuration provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating 2.0 GB of memory per core. The server operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the c6a.16xlarge in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, as well as PassMark CPU and memory scores. It exhibits strong performance in database operations, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. However, memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks (read and write) and single-threaded compression tasks fall into the middle 50% category. For language model tasks, prompt processing and text generation with a small 135M model are strong, whereas performance with medium 7B and large 70B models drops to average levels.

From a resource density perspective, the c6a.16xlarge offers a high-density compute profile with dedicated CPU allocation, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of local storage means all storage needs must be handled over the network, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. Additionally, the absence of AVX-512 support limits its efficiency in specific vector-heavy mathematical computations.

This server is designed for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, database operations, ray tracing, image processing, and high-throughput Redis caching. It is also suitable for small-scale language model inference and static web serving, though it is less optimal for memory-bound applications or large-scale LLM text generation.
